items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Happy Caldwell) does not mention Willie Cook. The interviewer mentions Willie Cook in the context of a misattribution of solos on Earl Hines records, which the interviewee does not address or confirm personal knowledge of.

ctx.x: Well, you know, there's -- Earl made some records about '40 -- oh, '46 or '47, and there's a couple of solos on those records, and a lot of people thought they were by Willie Cook, but Earl listened to them, and he told me they were by Billy Douglas. And he sort of (unintelligible).

Oh, he could play some beautiful chords. I [bought] -- when I left Philadelphia -- see, we go up to New York and visit. Came up wanted to visit a girlfriend of mine, and so -- okay, this place called a Hut. (Louis Metcalf had a (unintelligible) place on 145th Street where we all used to jam. So I called Louis (unintelligible), said, come on, Hap, says, glad to see you, because we were both writing for the Music Dial. And I said, Billy, let's go down
